title: VoiceOver (screen reader)
steps: Find the 'VoiceOver' switch at the top of the page.
Click the switch to turn it on.
The Mac will start speaking what is on the screen.
caution: VoiceOver changes how the keyboard and mouse behave. To turn it off at any time, hold the Command key and press F5 (on some keyboards, also hold the fn key).

title: Zoom (magnify the screen)
steps: Turn on 'Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom'.
Now hold Option and Command and press the equals key (=) to zoom in.
Hold Option and Command and press the minus key (-) to zoom out.

title: Make text bigger
steps: Drag the 'Preferred reading size' slider to the right to make text bigger.
Below it you can choose a size for each app, like Mail or Messages.
Click 'Done' when you're happy with it.

title: Increase contrast
steps: Turn on 'Increase contrast'.
Buttons and borders will get darker outlines so they stand out.

title: Reduce transparency
steps: Turn on 'Reduce transparency'.
See-through areas like the menu bar and sidebars will become solid.

title: Invert colors
steps: Turn on 'Invert colors'.
'Smart' keeps photos looking normal; 'Classic' inverts everything.

title: Color filters (color blindness)
steps: Turn on 'Color filters'.
Pick a 'Filter type', for example Grayscale or one for red/green color blindness.
Use 'Intensity' to make the effect stronger or weaker.

title: Bigger mouse pointer
steps: Drag the 'Pointer size' slider to the right to make the pointer bigger.

title: Shake to find the pointer
steps: Turn on 'Shake mouse pointer to locate'.
Now when you lose the pointer, wiggle the mouse or your finger quickly and it will grow for a moment.

title: Reduce motion
steps: Turn on 'Reduce motion'.
Sliding and zooming animations will be replaced with gentle fades.

title: Dim flashing lights
steps: Turn on 'Dim flashing lights'.
Videos with flashing or strobing lights will be dimmed automatically.

title: Read selected text aloud
steps: Turn on 'Speak selection'.
Now highlight any text, then hold Option and press Escape to hear it read aloud.
Change the voice with 'System voice'.

title: Speak what's under the pointer
steps: Turn on 'Speak item under the pointer'.
The Mac will read out whatever you rest the pointer on.

title: Hover Text (big text under the pointer)
steps: Turn on 'Hover Text'.
Hold the Command key while pointing at text to see it large in a bubble.

title: Accessibility shortcut
steps: Tick the features you want in the shortcut, for example VoiceOver or Zoom.
Then press Option, Command and F5 together at any time to turn them on or off.

title: Subtitles and captions
steps: Turn on 'Prefer closed captions and SDH' so videos show subtitles when they have them.
Pick a caption style from the list. 'Large Text' is easiest to read.

title: Live Captions (words on screen for any sound)
steps: Turn on 'Live Captions'.
A small box will appear that shows spoken words as text, from calls, videos or the room.
You can change the 'Font family' and colors below.

title: Hearing aids
steps: Make sure your hearing aids are on and nearby.
Wait for them to appear in the list, then click their name to connect.

title: Flash the screen for alerts
controlLabel: Flash the screen when an alert sound occurs
steps: Turn on 'Flash the screen when an alert sound occurs'.

title: Mono audio (one ear)
steps: Turn on 'Play stereo audio as mono'.
Both sides of your headphones will now play everything.

title: Background sounds (rain, ocean)
steps: Turn on 'Background sounds'.
Click 'Choose…' to pick a sound like Rain or Ocean.
Use 'Background sounds volume' to set how loud it is.

title: Headphone Accommodations
steps: Turn on 'Headphone Accommodations'.
Click 'Customize Audio' to tune the sound to your hearing.

title: Audio descriptions for videos
steps: Turn on 'Play audio descriptions when available'.

title: Sticky Keys (one key at a time)
keywords: press one key at a time
steps: Turn on 'Sticky Keys'.
Now you can press keys like Command, then the letter, one after the other instead of together.

title: Slow Keys (ignore accidental key presses)
steps: Turn on 'Slow Keys'.
Keys will only count when you hold them down a little longer.

title: On-screen keyboard
steps: Turn on 'Accessibility Keyboard'.
A keyboard will appear on screen that you can click with the mouse.

title: Full Keyboard Access (no mouse)
steps: Turn on 'Full Keyboard Access'.
Press Tab to move between buttons and Space to press them.

title: Mouse Keys (move pointer with keys)
steps: Turn on 'Mouse Keys'.
Use the number keys (or the keys around 'I' on a laptop) to move the pointer.

title: Double-click speed
steps: Drag the 'Double-click speed' slider to the left to give yourself more time between clicks.

title: Head pointer (move pointer with your head)
steps: Turn on 'Head pointer'.
The camera will follow your head movements to move the pointer.

title: Voice Control (control the Mac by voice)
steps: Turn on 'Voice Control'.
Say things like 'Open Mail' or 'Click Done'. Say 'Show commands' to see what you can say.

title: Live Speech (type to speak)
steps: Turn on 'Live Speech'.
Press Option, Command and F5 and choose Live Speech, then type and press Return to have the Mac say it out loud.

title: Switch Control
steps: Turn on 'Switch Control'.
Use 'Add' under Switches to set up the switch you use.

title: Wi-Fi
steps: Make sure the 'Wi-Fi' switch at the top is on (blue).
Click the name of your network in the list.
Type the Wi-Fi password when asked, then click 'Join'.

title: Bluetooth (headphones, speakers, mouse)
steps: Make sure the 'Bluetooth' switch at the top is on (blue).
Put your device in pairing mode (see its instructions; often you hold its power button).
When it appears under 'Nearby Devices', click 'Connect' next to it.

title: AirDrop (share with nearby Apple devices)
steps: Click the 'AirDrop' menu.
Choose 'Contacts Only' to receive from people you know, or 'Everyone for 10 Minutes' for anyone nearby.

title: Printers and scanners
steps: Make sure the printer is on and connected to the same Wi-Fi.
Click 'Add Printer, Scanner or Fax…'.
Choose your printer from the list and click 'Add'.

title: Sound output and volume
steps: Under 'Output', click the speakers or headphones you want to use.
Drag the 'Output volume' slider to the right to make it louder.
Make sure 'Mute' is not ticked.

title: Alert sound
steps: Click the 'Alert sound' menu and choose a sound you like.
Use the 'Alert volume' slider to make alerts louder or softer.

title: Startup chime
steps: Turn 'Play sound on startup' on or off.

title: Microphone level
steps: Click 'Input', then choose the microphone you want to use.
Drag the 'Input volume' slider to the right if people can't hear you.

title: Screen brightness
steps: Drag the 'Brightness' slider right to make the screen brighter, or left to make it darker.

title: Automatic brightness
steps: Turn 'Automatically adjust brightness' off if the screen keeps changing by itself.

title: True Tone (warmer screen colors)
steps: Turn 'True Tone' on or off. It makes colors look warmer in warm room light.

title: Night Shift (warmer screen at night)
steps: Scroll down and click 'Night Shift…'.
Choose a 'Schedule', for example 'Sunset to Sunrise'.
Drag 'Color temperature' toward 'More Warm' if you like.

title: Make everything on screen bigger
steps: Under the picture of your screen, click the option on the left, 'Larger Text'.
Everything on screen gets bigger. Pick one to the right if it's too big.

title: Dark Mode / Light Mode
steps: At the top next to 'Appearance', click 'Light', 'Dark' or 'Auto'.
'Auto' switches to dark in the evening.

title: Always show scroll bars
steps: Next to 'Show scroll bars', choose 'Always'.

title: Bigger sidebar icons
steps: Click the 'Sidebar icon size' menu and choose 'Large'.

title: Wallpaper (desktop picture)
steps: Click any picture to use it as your desktop picture.
To use your own photo, click 'Add Photo' or 'Add Folder' at the top.

title: Screen saver
steps: Click a screen saver to choose it.
To set when it starts, see the Lock Screen settings.

title: Dock size
steps: Drag the 'Size' slider toward 'Large' to make the Dock icons bigger.

title: Dock magnification
steps: Turn on 'Magnification'.
Drag its slider to choose how big icons grow when you point at them.

title: Hide or show the Dock
controlLabel: Automatically hide and show the Dock
steps: Turn off 'Automatically hide and show the Dock' to keep the Dock always visible.

title: Move the Dock
steps: Click the 'Position on screen' menu and choose Left, Bottom or Right.

title: Stage Manager
steps: Turn 'Stage Manager' on or off. It keeps recent windows in a strip on the left.

title: Default web browser
steps: Click the 'Default web browser' menu and choose the browser you want links to open in.

title: Hot Corners
steps: Scroll to the bottom and click 'Hot Corners…'.
Set a corner to '-' to stop it doing something when the pointer touches it.

title: Trackpad pointer speed
steps: Drag the 'Tracking speed' slider left to slow the pointer down, or right to speed it up.

title: Tap to click
steps: Turn 'Tap to click' on to click with a light tap, or off to stop accidental clicks.

title: Right-click (secondary click)
steps: Click the 'Secondary click' menu.
'Click with Two Fingers' is the usual choice; you can also pick a corner.

title: Click firmness
steps: Drag the 'Click' slider to 'Light' if clicking takes too much pressure.

title: Scroll direction
steps: Click the 'Scroll & Zoom' tab at the top.
Turn 'Natural scrolling' off if the page moves the opposite way you expect.

title: Key repeat
steps: Drag 'Key repeat rate' toward 'Off' or 'Slow'.
Drag 'Delay until repeat' toward 'Long' so held keys don't repeat so quickly.

title: Keyboard backlight
controlLabel: Adjust keyboard brightness in low light
steps: Turn 'Adjust keyboard brightness in low light' on or off.

title: Dictation (type by talking)
controlLabel: Use Dictation wherever you can type text
steps: Turn on the 'Dictation' switch.
In any place you can type, press the microphone key (or the 'Shortcut' shown) and start talking.

title: Text replacements
steps: Click 'Text Replacements…'.
Click '+' to add a short code that expands to a longer phrase, like your address.

title: Add a keyboard language
steps: Next to 'Input Sources', click 'Edit…'.
Click '+' and choose the language you want to type in.

title: Low Power Mode
steps: Click the 'Low Power Mode' menu and choose 'Only on Battery' or 'Always'.

title: Battery health and charging
steps: Click 'Options…' to see charging settings like 'Optimize Battery Charging'.
Next to 'Battery Health', click the 'i' button to see its condition.

title: When the screen turns off
steps: Click the 'Turn display off … when inactive' menu.
Choose a longer time, like 30 minutes, so the screen stays on longer.

title: Password after sleep
controlLabel: Require password after screen saver begins
steps: Click the 'Require password after screen saver begins or display is turned off' menu.
Choose how long to wait before the Mac asks for your password.

title: Lock screen message
steps: Turn on 'Show message when locked'.
Click 'Set…' and type something like 'If found, please call …'.

title: Touch ID (fingerprint)
controlLabel: Use Touch ID to unlock your Mac
steps: Click 'Add Fingerprint' and follow the steps, resting your finger on the Touch ID button.
Make sure 'Use Touch ID to unlock your Mac' is on.

title: Change your login password
steps: Next to 'Login password', click 'Change…'.
Type your old password, then the new one twice.

title: Log in automatically
steps: Click the 'Automatically log in as' menu and choose your name, or 'Off'.
caution: With automatic login, anyone who turns on this Mac can use it without a password.

title: FileVault (disk encryption)
steps: Scroll to 'FileVault' and click 'Turn On…'.
Write down the recovery key somewhere safe.
caution: If you forget your password and lose the recovery key, your files can't be recovered.

title: Location Services
steps: Turn 'Location Services' on or off at the top.
Below, turn it on or off for each app.

title: Which apps can use the camera
steps: Find the app in the list, like Zoom or FaceTime.
Turn its switch on to let it use the camera. You may need to quit and reopen the app.

title: Which apps can use the microphone
keywords: they can't hear me in zoom
steps: Find the app in the list.
Turn its switch on to let it use the microphone. You may need to quit and reopen the app.

title: Screen sharing permission for apps
steps: Find the app in the list.
Turn its switch on. The app will usually ask to quit and reopen.

title: Apps allowed to control the Mac
steps: Find the app in the list, for example AI Buddy.
Turn its switch on. You may be asked for your password.

title: Software updates
keywords: is my mac up to date
steps: Wait a moment while the Mac checks for updates.
If an update is listed, click 'Update Now' and keep the Mac plugged in.

title: Storage (free up space)
steps: Wait for the colored bar to show what's using space.
Look through the recommendations and categories below to remove things you don't need.

title: About this Mac
steps: Your Mac's name, chip, memory and macOS version are listed here.

title: Date and time
steps: Turn on 'Set time and date automatically' so the clock is always right.

title: 24-hour clock
steps: Turn '24-hour time' on or off.

title: Time zone
steps: Turn on 'Set time zone automatically using your current location', or pick a city below.

title: Language and region
steps: Click '+' under 'Preferred Languages' to add a language, then drag it to the top.
Use 'Region', 'Date format' and the temperature buttons below for local formats.

title: Apps that open at startup
steps: Under 'Open at Login', click an app and then the '–' button to stop it opening at startup.

title: Time Machine backups
steps: Plug in an external drive.
Click 'Add Backup Disk…' and choose the drive. Backups then happen automatically.

title: Notifications (pop-up messages)
steps: Scroll down to the list of apps and click the app that bothers you.
Turn off 'Allow notifications' to stop its pop-ups, or pick a quieter style.

title: Hide message previews
steps: Click the 'Show previews' menu and choose 'When Unlocked' or 'Never'.

title: Do Not Disturb / Focus
steps: Click 'Do Not Disturb'.
Add a schedule so it turns on by itself, for example overnight.

title: Siri
steps: Turn 'Siri' on.
Use 'Listen for' to choose whether saying 'Siri' wakes it up.

title: Downtime (screen-free hours)
steps: Turn on 'Downtime'.
Use 'Schedule' to choose the hours.

title: Show battery percentage
steps: Find 'Battery' in the list.
Turn on 'Show Percentage'.
